sport_summary: Massive 15-game MLB Wednesday slate headlines alongside NBA Playoffs, NHL, and even an early NFL future — with several sharp edges emerging in totals and spreads

picks.reasoning: The Under 7.5 at BetRivers shows a massive 250.8 edge_bps — the best line-value signal on the entire slate. Emerson Hancock takes the mound for Seattle, a ground-ball pitcher who limits hard contact, while Sean Burke for Chicago has shown inconsistency but pitches in a favorable environment here. The market median sits at -115, meaning BetRivers is offering significant value at -104 on a total that most books price much higher juice.

FanDuel's -102 on Atlanta -1.5 generates a blistering 188.6 edge_bps against a median of -110 — a massive pricing gap across the market. Chris Sale takes the mound for Atlanta against Janson Junk for Miami; Sale is a proven playoff-caliber arm and Junk is a fringe roster arm, making Atlanta's run-line coverage a high-probability outcome. This is elite value on a short spread with an elite starter.

The Over 6.5 at +102 on FanDuel posts a staggering 287.6 edge_bps, the single highest value signal in the entire dataset, against a median of -110 — a 212-basis-point gap that is almost certainly a stale or outlier price. Edward Cabrera for the Cubs and Kyle Harrison for Milwaukee are both capable of stretching games out, but a total set at 6.5 is extremely low and +102 odds represent pure value regardless of starter quality. Get this before the market corrects.

LowVig.ag offers +101 on the Over 10.5, generating 146.8 edge_bps against a median of -105 across 9 books — a 247-basis-point swing that signals a significant pricing error. This game is played at Coors Field, historically one of the highest-scoring environments in baseball, and both Kyle Freeland (who has struggled at altitude) and Jack Leiter are prone to elevated run totals. Getting plus-money on a total in Colorado is extremely rare value.

FanDuel's -104 on San Antonio +6.5 produces 140.1 edge_bps against a median of -110, a meaningful gap across 9 books. The Spurs moneyline at +215 implies they can hang in this game, and playoff underdogs frequently cover large spreads even in losses. OKC is a significant favorite but 6.5 is a lot of points to lay in a playoff context where the trailing team often controls the final margin.

BetMGM's -150 on Vegas +1.5 shows 153.8 edge_bps against a median of -160 across 9 books, and is the best available price on this puck-line. The Golden Knights at +162 ML are being priced as genuine contenders in a tight series, and covering +1.5 in a playoff hockey game is an extremely high-percentage outcome — Vegas loses by 1 or wins outright over 70% of the time in close postseason matchups. Solid value at the puck line given the competitive moneyline odds.

BetUS offers -116 on the Mets ML, generating a massive 185.2 edge_bps against a median of -125 across 9 books — a full 9-cent line discrepancy. Zach Thornton starts for the Mets against Zack Littell for Washington; the Nationals are a rebuilding club and Washington is among the weakest home-field advantages in the NL. Getting the favorite at -116 when the market consensus is -125 is straightforward closing-line value.
